newsitem.title: FINLAND: NEW AMER OWNER WANTS K FOR A SHR EXCHANGE.
newsitem.headline: NEW AMER OWNER WANTS K FOR A SHR EXCHANGE.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy on Tuesday detailed some terms that Jonathan Bryan Guinness, the third Lord Moyne, had set for his planned purchase of Amer K-shares unveiled on Monday.
The terms included an amendment to Amer's articles of association to make it possible to convert K-shares into A-shares at a one-for-one ratio, Amer said in a statement.
"Lord Moyne has accepted the offer of the K shareholders on the following essential terms and conditions set out in the agreement:
"(a) the decision-making bodies of the K shareholders shall approve the sale of at least 1,100,000 K shares in accordance with the offer;
"(b) the company shall not redeem the shares covered by the offer;
"(c) The Articles of Association of the company shall be amended, inter alia, so that the K shares of the company can be exchanged for A shares with a 1:1 ratio;
Lord Moyne expected formal approval from the K-shareholders by end-June, while the other conditions should be fulfilled by end-September, Amer said.

"Should the buyer not acquire all the K shares from the K shareholders, these shall have the obligation to exchange their remaining K shares for A shares in accordance with the amended articles of association," it said, adding the conversion could take place only provided that Lord Moyne exchanged his K shares for A shares.
